contentBody: **Which headline follows the rule for a first landing page?**
option.3: A short line that names the offer or the outcome
option.4: A paragraph of company history before any offer appears
answerExplanation: The headline is the first line a visitor reads. It should name the offer or outcome, not a generic welcome or a history essay.

contentBody: **After a chat tool drafts landing-page copy, what should you do first?**
option.1: Edit jargon and delete numbers or claims you did not supply
option.2: Publish the draft unchanged so the page stays fully automatic
option.3: Add fake ratings so the page looks already trusted
option.4: Replace the single button with login, shop, and blog links
answerExplanation: AI drafts words; you remain the editor. Invented counts, testimonials, and extra buttons should be removed before the page is shown.

contentBody: **What is a visual direction for a first prototype?**
option.1: The instruction make it look premium, with no subject or setting
option.2: A plain brief of subject, setting, and what to avoid in the picture
option.3: A claim that a generated person in the picture is a real customer
option.4: A requirement to fill the page with as many stock photos as possible
answerExplanation: Visuals should explain, not decorate. A useful brief names what to show and what not to show. Generated pictures are placeholders, not proof of real customers.
